title: Find out why the app sometimes dies at the start of a walk
goal: Now and then the app quits by itself in the first second of a scripted walk, inside a system accessibility message, before the walk has done anything. It has taken out at least four unrelated walks. Find out whether a person using the app could hit it too, and stop it.
notes: Seen 2026-09-26 06:22Z running Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/command-s-saves-a-video-project-walk.json --no-build: 'Verdict: CRASHED EXC_GUARD in static PhotonzApp.$main() < Photonz_main', log.json stopped after the setup step (forgot settings, copied the scratch b-roll). Report ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Photonz Probe-2026-09-25-232258.ips: EXC_GUARD GUARD_TYPE_MACH_PORT INVALID_OPTIONS on mach port 0; crashing thread main: mach_msg2_trap < mach_msg < HIServices _XMIGPostNotification < _AXUIElementPostNotificationWithInfo < AppKit _NSAccessibilityNotify < __CFRunLoopDoBlocks < NSApplication run. Same signature at 2026-09-25 22:32 (Photonz Probe-2026-09-25-223224.ips) and in sweeps: out-of-view-mark-walk (2026-09-21 06:00Z), multi-geometry-walk (11:16Z), each-corner-on-its-own-walk (grep EXC_GUARD queue/loop.log). The re-run of the same walk right after passed, so it is intermittent. Ghoztty Accessibility was denied on the Grants line each time; worth checking whether an AX notification posted while nothing is listening, or while the probe is not yet frontmost, is what trips the guard.
acceptance: The cause is named in this task's log with the evidence for it
Either it is fixed and the walks that hit it pass ten runs in a row, or it is shown to happen only under the walk harness and the harness stops provoking it

log.note: 2026-09-26: the probe died 2s after launch at 2026-09-25 23:22:53 (EXC_GUARD GUARD_TYPE_MACH_PORT INVALID_OPTIONS in mach_msg < _AXUIElementPostNotificationWithInfo < _NSAccessibilityNotify, run loop block; report ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Photonz Probe-2026-09-25-232258.ips; same signature 22:32:24). Its 'Photonz (Probe) quit unexpectedly' dialog then sat in front for 13 hours, so the probe could never become active and every walk's click on a timeline gesture did nothing (clicking-a-cut-opens-the-transition-picker-again). That makes these crashes costlier than one walk each: probe-app.sh now flags 'a system alert is in front' and failed walks say so.

Cause, with evidence: macOS kills the app while AppKit sends an accessibility notification to ANOTHER app that watches this one. The only observer on a test app here subscribes AXWindowCreated app-wide plus per-window TitleChanged/Moved/Destroyed, which is Ztabby's (AltTab-style) pattern (lldb on _XMIGPostNotification in a throwaway AppKit app, /tmp/axstress). _XMIGPostNotification does mach_msg(COPY_SEND, MACH_SEND_MSG|MACH_SEND_TIMEOUT) to the observer's port NAME. A 10-line C program sending that message to mach_task_self() / mach_thread_self() / a thread special reply port dies with EXC_GUARD GUARD_TYPE_MACH_PORT 'INVALID_OPTIONS on mach port 0 (guarded with 0x8001030400000011)', codes 0x9c00000/0x8001030400000011, byte-identical to all four probe reports (09-20 22:27, 09-21 03:39, 09-25 22:32, 09-25 23:22). Sends to port 0, a dead name, a plain receive right or a send-once right just return MACH_SEND_INVALID_DEST. So HIServices sent to an observer name that had died and been reused for one of the app's own kernel objects: a macOS bug, which mpv #12632 and zed #9261 also hit. Nothing in Photonz sends that message.

Could a person hit it: yes, in principle, any Photonz build while a window-watching app (the user's own Ztabby) runs, mostly in the first seconds after launch. The rate is about 4 in several thousand probe launches over a week, and the Dev app has no such report in the retained week (09-20 to 09-27). 130 launches of the throwaway app with Ztabby watching (windows plus thread-port churn) did not reproduce it, so there is no faster trigger. There is nothing to fix in Photonz; if the user wants it gone at the source, it is on Ztabby's side (per-window observers created and dropped at launch) or Apple's.

Harness now stops being hurt by it: Scripts/crash-report.mjs recognises the shape (macos-ax-notify: EXC_GUARD + GUARD_TYPE_MACH_PORT + INVALID_OPTIONS + _XMIGPostNotification/_AXUIElementPostNotification on the faulting thread) and says 'a macOS fault, not the app' instead of blaming PhotonzApp.$main; playtest.sh reruns such a walk once ('==> First try: CRASHED ...', not a Verdict), and playtest-all prints 'ok  on a rerun: the first try hit a macOS fault'. A second fault in a row is CRASHED as before. Drill: node Scripts/crash-report-drill.mjs (6 new checks, incl. same guard from our own code NOT excused). End-to-end: SIGKILLed the probe mid-walk with a restamped copy of the real report in PHOTONZ_CRASH_REPORTS_DIR: one kill -> ok on a rerun, two kills -> CRASHED. The four walks it hit (command-s-saves-a-video-project, out-of-view-mark, multi-geometry, each-corner-on-its-own) passed 10 runs in a row each, 40/40. Scripts/test.sh green (10,125 tests).

left rough: Photonz Probe-2026-09-26-060353.ips is a different crash: EXC_CRASH (SIGSEGV), zero codes, 1.4s after launch, main thread idle in the run loop and no thread in app code. Seen once, not reproduced, no queue task mentions it; it did not earn a task. If it shows up again it can be filed then. Also the 'quit unexpectedly' dialog a real fault leaves is still up during the rerun; probe-app.sh already flags it on the Grants line, and a walk that needs clicks on the timeline may fail behind it.

Cause named and proven: macOS kills the app while AppKit posts an accessibility notification to a window-watching app (Ztabby) by a port name reused for one of the app's own kernel objects; a C program sending HIServices' message to mach_task_self() dies with the byte-identical guard. Not Photonz code; a person could hit it too with such an app running, about once in thousands of launches. Harness (3f1274cc): crash-report.mjs names it a macOS fault, playtest.sh reruns the walk once, playtest-all says ok on a rerun; drill + two end-to-end kill drills; the four walks it hit passed 10/10 each; Scripts/test.sh green.
